info.title: Car Wash API
info.summary: Bookings, shifts, geofenced attendance and per-wash bonuses.
info.description:
Every response is the same envelope: `{ "success": true, "data": ... }` on success, `{ "success": false, "error": { "domain", "code", "message" } }` on failure. **Branch on `error.code`, never on `error.message`** — the code is a stable contract, the message is prose and may be reworded or translated.

The surface is segmented by audience, and the segmentation is the authorisation: `/customer/*`, `/employee/*` and `/manager/*` each admit exactly one role. A token for the wrong role gets `403 FORBIDDEN`, not a filtered response. Response shapes differ by audience on purpose — a customer's reservation carries no `bonus_mnt` and no other customer's phone number, while a staff reservation carries both. They are separate schemas here because they are separate types in the service.

**This service is now multi-tenant.** Every `/api/v1` path requires the `X-API-Key` header identifying the business, in addition to the bearer token identifying the person. The key is resolved against the platform, which in the same call returns the tenant's subscription and module entitlement - so every path can also answer 402 (the plan does not permit it) and 503 (the platform could not be reached to find out). Paths are otherwise unchanged.

It runs as its own deployment and talks to the platform over HTTP. Mounting it in-process instead would add a `/carwash` prefix and change nothing else. See `docs/ADOPTING-INTO-CORE.md`.

tags.name: Operational
tags.description: Unversioned. Describes the deployment rather than serving its data.

tags.name: Public
tags.description: No credentials. Sign-in and the price list a visitor could read off a wall.

tags.name: Employee
tags.description: Requires an employee token. Every route is scoped to the caller — none takes an employee id.

tags.name: Manager
tags.description: Requires a manager token. The only audience that reads other people's data.

get.description: Deliberately dependency-free. A health check that queries the database turns a slow query into a restart loop.

get.summary: What this deployment can actually do
get.description: Answers 200 with `degraded: true` rather than a failure status: a deployment missing an optional feature is degraded, not unhealthy, and a 503 here would make an orchestrator restart a process working exactly as configured. Alert on `degraded`.

post.summary: Create a customer account and sign in
post.description:
Customers only. There is no `role` field: an endpoint that took one would be one validation slip away from letting anyone mint a manager. Staff accounts are created by a manager via `POST /manager/staff`.

Rate limited (`AUTH_RATE_PER_MINUTE`).

Three outcomes, not one. A phone number nobody has booked with creates an ordinary account. A phone number with guest bookings PLUS a matching `reference` upgrades that guest record in place, so every booking made under the number is there from the first sign-in. A phone number with guest bookings and no reference is refused with the two things that work - because silently creating an empty account would hide the bookings, and without this branch the unique index on the derived contact key refuses the insert and the error blames the email address, which is neither true nor fixable by the person reading it.

A wrong reference, and a right one with the wrong number, both give the same 404 the lookup gives: signing up must not become the oracle the lookup refuses to be.

409.description: That email is already registered. Confirms the address exists — an accepted trade for not leaving someone unable to sign in with no explanation; the rate limit is what stops bulk enumeration.

post.summary: Exchange credentials for a bearer token
post.description:
An unknown email and a wrong password return the identical 401, wording included. Distinguishing them turns this into a "does this person have an account here" oracle.

Rate limited (`AUTH_RATE_PER_MINUTE`); a 429 carries `Retry-After` in seconds.

403.description: The account is suspended. Checked after the password, so the answer leaks nothing to someone guessing addresses.

get.description: Active services only, and without `bonus_mnt` — what the company pays its staff per job is not part of a price list. The manager's `GET /manager/services` is a different response type.
Includes each site's coordinate and clock-in radius: the apps need them to show a site on a map and to measure a clock-in against it before asking.

The trading name of whichever business the `X-API-Key` belongs to.

Token-free because the storefront needs a name before anyone signs in - a visitor reading the price list has not got a token and never will. It costs the server nothing: resolving the tenant already fetched and cached this, so the value is read off the request rather than looked up again.

A client should prefer this over a name compiled into its own build. A rename in the platform console then reaches every storefront on the next cache refresh, instead of each one carrying a copy nobody remembers to change.

Active photographs only, in display order.

Public because the shopfront is: there is nothing private in a picture a business chose to put on its own home page, and requiring a token would mean the marketing site cannot draw before somebody signs in - which is every visitor, every time.

Withdrawn images are absent here and still present in the manager's list, which is the whole difference between the two.

get.summary: The people a visitor may choose between
get.description:
Active employees, as id and display name only.

Public because booking is. Choosing who washes your car means seeing who there is, and a customer who has not registered has no other way to be shown it - so requiring a token here would mean requiring registration, which is the thing guest booking exists to remove.

This returns EmployeeCard and not the personnel record: no address, no telephone number, no employment status, no home site. The full roster - who is on shift where and when - stays on the manager surface.

get.summary: Who can do this service on this day, and when
get.description:
Free slots for a named service on a named day.

Public for the same reason as the employee list: it is what a person needs in order to pick a time, and they do not have an account yet.

`day` is read in the BUSINESS timezone, not the caller's. A customer in another offset asking for Tuesday means the shop's Tuesday.

parameters.name: service_id
parameters.description: Which service, because its duration decides which slots fit.

post.summary: Book a wash without an account
post.description:
A phone number, a plate, and the slot. No registration, no password, no token.

Requiring an account before the first booking asks somebody to commit to a relationship with a business they have not bought anything from yet; the usual result is that they telephone instead, or go elsewhere.

This is NOT a second booking system. The roster check, the overlap check, the unique slot key that stops two customers taking one time, and the price and bonus copied at booking time are the same code that serves a signed-in customer. What differs is only who the customer is and how they were identified.

The phone number is find-or-create: booking again with the same number is recognised as the same customer, so a business accumulates a real history rather than a pile of one-visit strangers. The plate does the same for the car. An existing REGISTERED customer is reused too - somebody who cannot remember their password should not end up with their history split in two.

A phone number proves nothing, and nothing here treats it as proof. It groups bookings; it is never on its own permission to read one back.

RATE LIMITED, and that is not a formality: this is the only unauthenticated route in the service that writes. A signed-in customer filling a calendar with nonsense has an account to suspend; an anonymous caller has nothing, so the limiter is the only thing between a business's day and whoever decides to fill it.

The response carries the reference code, and it is the only time it is ever sent. Show it to the customer.

phone.description: Dashes, spaces and a leading + are accepted; it is reduced to its digits before it is stored or compared, so the same person writing it a different way is still the same person.

name.description: Optional. A business would like it, but refusing the booking over it loses the sale for a field that is decoration on a car wash: the plate identifies the car and the phone reaches the person.

get.summary: Find a booking with its reference and phone number
get.description:
BOTH are required, and each covers the other's weakness.

The reference is the secret - but it is a secret that gets screenshotted, forwarded and left in chat threads. The phone number is not a secret at all - but it is something only the person who booked and the business know to pair with that code.

A wrong reference, and a right reference with the wrong number, give the SAME 404. That is not politeness. Distinguishing them would turn this into an oracle for testing whether a code is real, and the code space is only worth anything while it cannot be probed. For the same reason the route is rate limited even though it only reads.

Registering an account is the other way to find a booking, and the one to use for a history rather than a single visit.

parameters.name: reference
parameters.description: With or without the dash, in any case.

parameters.name: phone
parameters.description: The number the booking was made with, written any way.

get.summary: Who am I signed in as
get.description: The one authenticated route that is not audience-specific: any role may call it.

post.description: The owner is the authenticated caller; there is no `owner_id` field to point at somebody else. The plate is uppercased and stripped of spaces before storage, and is unique per owner — not globally, because a plate changes hands and refusing the new owner would be a support ticket with no good answer.

409.description: This owner already has that plate

get.description: Scoped to the owner in the query itself. Another customer's car answers **404, not 403** — a 403 would confirm the id is real, which turns id guessing into a census of registered vehicles.

put.description: Only the fields present are changed; a blank string is treated as "leave it alone".

409.description: This owner already has that plate

get.description: Scoped to the caller in the query. There is no `customer_id` parameter on this route, so there is nothing to tamper with.

post.summary: Book a wash with a chosen washer
post.description:
Availability is **re-derived server-side** rather than trusting the slot list the client was shown, which may be minutes stale. On top of that, a unique index on (employee, start instant) makes the database refuse the second of two simultaneous bookings for the same slot.

`price_mnt` and `bonus_mnt` are copied onto the booking at this moment and never read through afterwards: editing the price list must not rewrite revenue already banked or a bonus already earned.

Rate limited (`BOOKING_RATE_PER_MINUTE`).

404.description: The car is not the caller's, or the service, location or employee does not exist

post.description: Frees the slot for someone else. Only an open booking can be cancelled; a completed wash answers 409.

409.description: It can no longer be cancelled

get.description: **Not clocked in is `200` with `data: null`, not 404.** It is an ordinary state the app renders a button for; making the normal case an error status forces every client to special-case it.

post.summary: Start a shift, if you are on site
post.description:
Refused outside the site's `geofence_radius_m` with **`422 OUTSIDE_GEOFENCE`**, and the message carries the measured and permitted distances — so a client can say "you are 240 m away" rather than "invalid request". Five metres over is GPS drift worth waiting out; three kilometres is the wrong branch, and only the number distinguishes them.

A coordinate of exactly `(0, 0)` is treated as "no fix yet" and reported as a validation failure, not as being far away: a phone without a fix reports Null Island, and telling that person they are at the wrong site is a lie.

At most one open entry per employee, enforced by a unique index as well as a service check — a read-then-write races with itself when two taps arrive together.

**Never refused for being far from the site.** The distance is measured and stored, but blocking it would leave someone who has already gone home clocked in indefinitely, inflating their hours and needing a manager to fix by hand. A clock-out from the wrong place is a question for a person to look at, which is what recording the distance makes possible.

`clock_out_distance_m` is `-1` when the device gave no usable fix — not `0`, which would read as standing exactly on the site.

get.description:
Same response type as the manager's `GET /manager/timesheets`, deliberately: a manager reviewing a disputed shift should be looking at the record the employee is looking at, distances included.

An open entry contributes zero minutes and is counted separately in `open_entries` — a timesheet that reads low usually has one, and folding it into the total hides the reason.

Returned as `StaffReservation`: the same booking the customer sees, plus what it pays and the customer's number to call if they are late. Both are appropriate here and neither appears on the customer's own view.

put.summary: Move one of the caller's own jobs on
put.description:
Confined to the caller's own work: another employee's booking answers 404, the same as one that does not exist. Without that, any employee could mark any other's wash complete, crediting the bonus to the wrong person invisibly until payroll.

Transitions: `booked` → `in_progress` | `completed` | `cancelled` | `no_show`; `in_progress` → `completed` | `cancelled`. Everything else is terminal, because each of those has already affected a report. Completing writes `completed_at`, which is what the daily report groups on.

409.description: That transition is not allowed from the current status

post.summary: Add a washer or a manager
post.description:
`role` is a field here, unlike on public registration, because the caller is already a manager. `customer` is still refused: an account created by someone else, with a password that person chose, is not an account that customer agreed to.

An employee requires `home_location_id`, and it is checked against the collection — an employee rostered to a site that does not exist passes every later check and then fails at clock-in, far from the cause.

Rate limited (`AUTH_RATE_PER_MINUTE`), since it sets a password.

404.description: The home location does not exist

put.description:
Takes effect on the target's **next request**, not on their next login: the auth middleware loads the user from the database on every call rather than trusting the token's claims. Suspension that waits for a token to expire is not suspension.

A manager suspending their own account is refused — it locks the business out of its own back office and the fix needs database access.

422.description: Unknown status, or a manager suspending themselves

get.description: The one route that returns a list of customers with their email and phone. Manager-only for that reason.
Withdrawn entries included — the likeliest reason to open this screen is to bring one back — and with `bonus_mnt`, which the public list omits.

post.description: `bonus_mnt` above `price_mnt` is refused: it means every completed wash loses money, which is almost always a missing or extra zero, and catching it here is cheaper than finding it in a month of payroll.

put.description: Changing a price leaves every existing booking untouched — each copied the price it was sold at. Yesterday's report will not move. Setting `active: false` removes it from the customer app immediately and leaves the history intact.

post.description: `geofence_radius_m` must be between 25 and 1000. The floor exists because consumer GPS is routinely 10–20 m out and worse beside a building: a tighter fence is not a strict policy, it is a clock-in that fails at random for people standing in the right place. Past a kilometre the fence stops meaning "at work" and starts meaning "in the district".

get.description: Returns shifts that **overlap** the window, not shifts that start inside it. The difference shows on a 22:00–02:00 shift: asking which shifts start today drops it from tomorrow, even though tomorrow's first two hours are covered — and availability is built from this list, so the employee would look unbookable for hours they are working.

post.description: Its slots become bookable at once — the roster is the only source of availability. One employee cannot hold two overlapping shifts: the second is refused, because a roster that says otherwise offers bookings at both sites. A shift longer than 16 hours is refused as a probable wrong date on the end time.

404.description: The employee or location does not exist

409.description: That employee already has an overlapping shift

delete.description: Its slots stop being offered immediately. Bookings already taken inside it are **not** cancelled — that is a decision for a person, not a side effect of editing a roster.

get.description: Unlike the employee's own list, this one takes `employee_id`: seeing anyone's work is the manager's job.

post.summary: Register a car that is on the forecourt now
post.description:
The desk, not the website. Somebody has driven in, the manager has thirty seconds and a queue behind them, and the only thing they can read off the car is its plate. So the form is a plate, a service and a washer; the time is now, the job starts immediately, and the customer is whoever owns that plate.

Three rules the online flow enforces are deliberately relaxed here:

1. The start time is now rather than in the future. Online that would be a mistake; here it is the point.
2. The roster is not consulted. A walk-in arrives when it arrives, and refusing to record work that is visibly happening because nobody rostered that hour sends the manager to a paper notebook - and from that moment the day report is no longer true.
3. Overlap with the washer's other jobs is allowed. A manager standing in front of both cars knows something the roster does not.

What is NOT relaxed: a suspended employee is refused, an inactive service or location is refused, and the price and bonus are copied from the catalogue at registration time. Those are not scheduling rules - they are what makes the row correct afterwards.

The plate is find-or-create. A plate the business has seen keeps its existing owner, so a registered customer who drives in today gets this wash in the history they already have. A plate nobody has seen gets a customer of its own named after it: a reservation needs a customer, and one shared 'walk-in' account would make every returning driver indistinguishable in the list a manager uses to recognise them.

Separate from POST /bookings on purpose. That route is open to the internet and rate limited per IP, so one busy desk would trip the limiter from a single address, and it insists on a telephone number - the field this exists to avoid asking for.

plate.description: Spaces are removed and letters upper-cased before it is stored or compared, so the same plate typed differently is still the same car.

put.summary: Hand an open job to a different washer
put.description:
This is the point at which the bonus changes hands, which is why it is manager-only. Availability is re-checked for the new washer, so an off-shift or already-booked target is refused with `409 SLOT_UNAVAILABLE` saying which.

**A completed job cannot be reassigned.** The bonus has already been earned by whoever did the work, and moving it would silently change a report someone has already read.

409.description: Not an open booking, or the new washer is not free

put.description: Same state machine as the employee route, without the own-work restriction.

get.description: The same response type the employee sees of themselves, across everybody and filterable.

Grouped on `completed_at`, **not** on booking time: a wash booked for 17:45 and finished at 18:20 belongs to the day it was paid for, and a job that ran past midnight belongs to the day it finished. Reporting by booking time would put revenue on a day no money was taken.

Employees who were on site but completed nothing still appear, with zero washes — dropping them would make this a list of today's earners rather than today's staff. `worked_minutes` and `washes` are independent figures and neither is derived from the other; an employee still clocked in shows zero minutes with washes on the board.

Rows are ordered by revenue then id, so the order is stable across refreshes.

parameters.name: day
parameters.description: `YYYY-MM-DD` in the business timezone. Defaults to today.

get.description: Not active-only, unlike the public list: the likeliest reason to open this screen is to bring a withdrawn photograph back, and a list that hides them makes that impossible.

post.description:
A multipart form: the file, and everything about it, in one request.

One request rather than upload-then-describe, because a two-step flow leaves an undescribed image behind every time somebody closes the tab - and the description is the only thing a screen reader has.

The type is decided by SNIFFING the bytes, never by the declared Content-Type: a declared type is a claim about a file, not a fact about it, and the two differ exactly when it matters. SVG is refused - it carries script. The destination folder is derived from the resolved tenant and the object name is random, so a caller cannot choose where its file lands or overwrite somebody else's.

`402 LIMIT_EXCEEDED` when the plan caps gallery images and the cap is reached. Hero and about are never capped: a plan that forbids a business from having a home page cover is not a tier, it is a broken site.

alt_mn.description: Description in Mongolian. At least one language is required.

put.summary: Set the display order of several photographs
put.description: One call rather than one per tile. Dragging a photograph to the front of a twelve-image gallery renumbers most of them, and twelve requests racing each other is how a grid ends up in an order nobody chose.

ids.description: Image ids in the order they should appear.

put.summary: Change a photograph's description, placement or visibility
put.description:
The bytes are NOT editable. Replacing an image is an upload and a delete, so a URL a customer has already loaded never silently becomes a different picture.

Moving an image into `hero` or `about` demotes whichever image held that role to `gallery`.

active.description: false withdraws it from the storefront and keeps it in the back office.

delete.description: The record goes first, then the file at the image host. That order on purpose: a failure after the row is gone leaves one orphaned object, which costs a little storage and is invisible, while the other order risks a row pointing at a file that is already gone - a broken image on a customer's screen.

get.description: Everything the manager may see on a single booking, including the bonus and the customer's telephone number. Exists so a detail screen has its own address: reachable from a phone list, a link in a message or a bookmark, rather than only by finding the row again in whichever day was on screen.

put.description:
Three fields, each one a mistake somebody actually makes at a desk: the plate was mistyped, the wrong service was tapped, or the car went in half an hour before anyone registered it.

Send only what changed. Every field is optional and an absent one is left alone, so a screen that edits the plate does not have to send - and risk clobbering - the other two.

Changing the service re-copies the price and the bonus from the catalogue, and recomputes the end time from the new duration. Changing the start time recomputes the end time too. Changing the plate moves the booking to that car, and the customer moves with it: a booking belongs to whoever owns the vehicle being washed.

Unlike /assign, this is allowed on a COMPLETED booking. A correction that cannot be applied to yesterday is not a correction, it is a second wrong number sitting next to the first. The day report is computed from these rows, so yesterday's figure changes when yesterday's row does - including a washer's bonus. That is intended, and it is why this route is manager-only.

A cancelled or no-show booking cannot be edited. Nothing happened, so there is nothing to correct; registering the wash again is both easier to do and easier to read afterwards.

The roster is not consulted and overlap is not checked, for the same reason as the walk-in desk: the manager is the one holding the information. The slot key still applies while the booking is open, so two jobs cannot land on one washer at one instant.

schema.description: At least one field. Anything omitted is left unchanged.

409.description: The booking was cancelled, or that washer already has a job at that instant

bearerAuth.description: From `POST /api/v1/auth/login`. The claim set is only the subject and role; the role is re-read from the database on every request, so a change of role or a suspension takes effect on the next call rather than the next login.

tenantKey.name: X-API-Key
tenantKey.description:
The tenant API key, issued by the platform. It identifies WHICH business the request is for; the bearer token identifies which person within it. Both are required on every /api/v1 route and neither substitutes for the other.

It is resolved against the platform on each request (cached), and that one call also returns the tenant's subscription and module entitlement - so an unknown key is 401, a plan without the car wash is 402 MODULE_NOT_ENTITLED, and a lapsed subscription is 402 SUBSCRIPTION_REQUIRED on mutating calls only.

Keep it server-side. It is not a public value: anyone holding it can read that business's bookings, staff and day report.

From.name: from
From.description: `YYYY-MM-DD` in the business timezone. Defaults to today.

To.name: to
To.description: `YYYY-MM-DD`, **inclusive** — 1st to 7th contains the 7th. Defaults to `from`. The window may not exceed 92 days; an unbounded range is a collection scan one bookmarked URL can repeat all day.

Forbidden.description: Authenticated, but the wrong role for this audience — or the account is suspended. Carries no detail: telling a customer that a route needs the manager role maps the private surface for them.

NotFound.description: No such row, or it belongs to someone else — the two are deliberately indistinguishable on owner-scoped routes

ValidationFailed.description: The body parsed but its values are not acceptable

RateLimited.description: Too many requests from this client. `Retry-After` gives the wait in seconds.

OutsideGeofence.description: Too far from the site to clock in. `error.code` is `OUTSIDE_GEOFENCE` and `error.message` carries both the measured and the permitted distance. Distinct from a plain validation failure because the client acts on it differently: the right response is "move closer", not "fix your input".

SlotUnavailable.description: The washer is not free for the whole window — off shift, already booked, or the service would run past the end of their shift. `error.code` is `SLOT_UNAVAILABLE`.

PaymentRequired.description:
The tenant's plan does not permit this. `error.code` distinguishes the three cases: MODULE_NOT_ENTITLED (the plan does not include the car wash at all), SUBSCRIPTION_REQUIRED (it does, but the subscription has lapsed - mutating calls only), LIMIT_EXCEEDED (a numeric ceiling on the plan, such as the number of sites).

Reads are deliberately NOT refused for a lapsed subscription: a business behind on payment must still be able to see its data and reach the screen that explains the bill.

PlatformUnavailable.description:
The platform could not be reached to resolve this tenant, and nothing was cached for it. `error.code` is UPSTREAM_ERROR.

Deliberately NOT a 402. An unreachable platform means we could not find out what this tenant is entitled to - not that they are unentitled - and reporting it as non-payment would tell paying customers they had not paid. When a cached answer is available it is served instead, and `/readyz` reports the link as degraded.

message.description: Kept alongside `error` because existing clients read it. New clients branch on `error.code`.

domain.description: The subsystem the failure came from. Useful for alerting: "every 5xx today is ATTENDANCE" is far more actionable than "the API is throwing 500s".

message.description: Prose. Safe to show a user; never branch on it.

stack_trace.description: Development only. Never present in production.

ErrorCode.description:
The closed set of codes this API returns. Clients branch on these.

SUBSCRIPTION_REQUIRED, MODULE_NOT_ENTITLED and LIMIT_EXCEEDED are all 402 and all arrived with adoption into the platform. They are 402 rather than 403 because the caller is not permanently barred - they are one plan change away - so the right response is an upgrade prompt, not an apology. A client written before adoption will not have handled them.

timezone.description: The IANA zone every report and `?day=` is cut on. Clients must format dates in this zone, not the browser's.

degraded.description: True when any optional feature is switched off. Alert on this: silent degradation is how a feature stays off for a week with nobody noticing.

detail.description: Present only when disabled. Names the variable to set, not the symptom.

MNT.description: Whole tugrik. There is no minor unit and no scaling factor — the integer IS the amount. Never a float: the daily report sums hundreds of these and rounding would show up in the line an employee reads to check their own bonus.

EmployeeCard.description: An employee as a CUSTOMER sees them: enough to choose a person, and nothing more.

StaffMember.description: A person as a MANAGER sees them — the full personnel record. Never returned on a customer route.

geofence_radius_m.description: How far from (lat, lng) a clock-in is accepted. Per-site, not a global constant: a forecourt works at 75 m while a bay inside a shopping centre needs 200 m before honest staff start failing on indoor GPS drift.

WashService.description: A service as a CUSTOMER sees it. No bonus.

duration_min.description: Drives availability: a slot is offered only when this whole duration fits inside a shift.

allOf.description: What the assigned employee earns for completing one. A flat amount per wash rather than a percentage of the price: the employee does the same work whether or not the customer had a discount, and a percentage makes every price change silently a pay change.

notes.description: The owner's own note. Absent from CarBrief, which staff see — it is a note to self, not an instruction to the washer.

CarBrief.description: The vehicle on a job card: what staff need to find it in the queue.

NamedRef.description: An id with the label a UI shows for it, so a client needs no second map to render a list.

Reservation.description: A booking as its own CUSTOMER sees it. **`bonus_mnt` is absent, and that is why this schema exists separately from StaffReservation** — what the company pays the washer is between the company and the washer.

allOf.description: The same job as an EMPLOYEE or MANAGER sees it: what it pays, and who to call. Never returned on a customer route — it carries another customer's phone number.

slots.description: Always an array, never null. **Empty means working but fully booked** — someone not rostered that day is absent from the enclosing list instead.

clock_in_distance_m.description: Metres from the site when clocking in. Kept, not just the pass/fail verdict: when someone disputes a rejected clock-in the only useful record is where the phone said they were.

clock_out_distance_m.description: `-1` when the device gave no usable fix — not `0`, which would read as standing on the site.

worked_minutes.description: Written once, at clock-out. Zero while the entry is running.

open_entries.description: Surfaced rather than folded into the total. An open entry contributes zero minutes, so a timesheet with one reads low for a reason the reader cannot otherwise see — and the usual cause is somebody who forgot to clock out.

name.description: `(removed employee)` when the account is gone — a deleted employee still owns the work they did.

worked_minutes.description: From the timesheet, not from the washes. Zero with washes on the board means the entry is still open.

day.description: Echoed as `YYYY-MM-DD`, not a timestamp: a client that re-derives the date in its own timezone would display a different day than it asked for.

net_mnt.description: Revenue less bonus. Carried rather than left to the client to subtract, so two clients cannot disagree about it.

reference.description:
OPTIONAL. The code from a booking made without an account.

A guest who has booked already HAS a customer record - keyed by their phone number, holding their bookings - so the account must become THAT record rather than a new one beside it, or the history is stranded on a row nobody can sign in to. This code, together with `phone`, is how ownership is proved, and it is checked by the same code path the public booking lookup uses rather than by a second implementation written for signup.

employee_id.description: Chosen by the customer. This is what ties the bonus to a person.

start_at.description: RFC 3339. Must be in the future and within `MAX_BOOKING_DAYS_AHEAD`. Use a `start_at` taken from an availability slot.

ClockOutRequest.description: Coordinates are recorded but never gate the call.

role.description: `customer` is refused — customers sign themselves up.

Business.description:
The tenant's display identity, as the storefront renders it.

Deliberately just the two fields. The server holds the whole entitlement for this request - which modules the plan includes, its numeric limits, when the billing period ends - and none of that belongs on a page an anonymous visitor can read. Those are the operator's commercial details; the fact that they sit in the same struct server-side is not a reason to publish them.

slug.description: Short handle the platform files this business under.

MediaRole.description:
Where a photograph appears.

A role, not a position in a list. The site used to take its home page cover from photos[0] and its about-section image from photos[4], which meant the cover was not something anybody could set - it was whichever photograph sorted first, and changing it meant reordering an album until the right one landed at the top.

`hero` and `about` hold at most one image per business. Promoting a second one DEMOTES the previous holder to `gallery` rather than being refused: replacing is what the person meant.

Media.description:
An uploaded photograph.

One response shape for both audiences, unlike reservations - a photograph on a public page has no private half. What differs between the manager and a visitor is WHICH rows each is shown, which is a filter and not a shape. The image host's internal handle is deliberately absent: it is of no use to a client and a field that does not exist cannot be added to a response by accident.

url.description: Where the image is served from.

width.description: Intrinsic pixel width, taken from the upload response rather than asked of whoever uploaded it. Without it every photograph shifts the page as it loads, and a number a person types is the one nobody checks.

alt.description: Describes the photograph for somebody who cannot see it, keyed by locale. Never decorative: these are pictures of work, and this is the only description of what the picture shows. Sent as the whole locale map rather than resolved to one language, because the site switches language without a round trip.

tag.description: Groups a gallery photograph under one filter. Absent for hero and about, which are not filtered.

feature.description: A tile that takes more room in the grid.

active.description: A withdrawn photograph stays in the back office so it can be brought back, and is not served to the public list.

reference.description:
The code that finds this booking again.

Sent on the booking response and on a successful lookup, and NOWHERE else. No route will reveal the code for a booking the caller cannot already identify, because the code is the only thing standing between a phone number - which is not a secret, and which anybody can type - and the booking behind it.

Drawn from an alphabet that excludes both halves of every confusable pair (0/O, 1/I/L, 2/Z, 5/S, 8/B), so a code read off a screen and typed by somebody else cannot be silently mistaken for a different real one. Shown with a dash for reading aloud; the dash is not part of the value and is accepted with or without it, in any case.

GuestBooking.description:
A booking as the person who made it sees it, without an account.

Deliberately does NOT name the customer. Whoever reads this either booked it or was given the code and the phone number by somebody who did, so repeating their name back tells the reader nothing they did not have - and is one more thing to leak the day a screenshot is forwarded.
